note: Re-encoded on 29 Oct 2026 (change C6) to follow the selection framework as revised after the full synthesis of 35 sources (Theron, DST481, Table 4.5). Magnitude rule: the largest weight a factor may carry depends on the confidence in its evidence -- up to 3 for moderate or high confidence, at most 1 for low confidence or a design assumption. Changes from 1.1.0: (1) regulation is rated low confidence and the evidence no longer supports favouring plan-driven methods (Ribeiro et al. 2025; Smith et al. 2019 report adapted agile processes meeting regulatory demands), so its weights are capped at +/-1 and no longer separate plan-driven from adapted agile or hybrid processes under strict regulation; (2) the coordination guidance for large projects (high confidence; Kula et al. 2022, Berntzen et al. 2023, Bick et al. 2018) and the training and change-management guidance for low maturity (high confidence; McKenzie et al. 2021, Uludag et al. 2019, Dikert et al. 2016) now apply whichever methodology is recommended; (3) the regulation caveat now cites the empirical sources and covers the hybrid. Weights for requirement_volatility, team_size, release_frequency, team_maturity and distributed_team are unchanged; release_frequency's evidence is now rated moderate (Forsgren et al. 2018; Offerman et al. 2022; Lopez-Fernandez et al. 2022) but its weights already used the full range.

plan_driven.label: Plan-driven (Waterfall / V-Model)
plan_driven.rationale: Suits stable requirements and infrequent releases (Table 4.5; Findings 1.1, 2.1). For strict regulation it is one acceptable option among adapted agile and hybrid processes, not the only one (Finding 2.3, low confidence).

scrum.label: Scrum
scrum.rationale: Iterative delivery for small teams facing changing requirements (Table 4.5: volatile requirements and small team favour an iterative method; Findings 1.1, 1.2, 2.1).

kanban.label: Kanban
kanban.rationale: Continuous flow with work-in-progress limits; suited to unpredictable, steady demand (Table 4.5: volatile requirements and small team favour an iterative method -- Scrum or Kanban; Findings 1.1, 2.1).

agile_devops.label: Agile with DevOps (CI/CD)
agile_devops.rationale: Frequent releases with automated build, test and deployment; demands technical maturity (Table 4.5: frequent releases and a mature team favour Agile with DevOps and delivery measures; Finding 3.2: Forsgren et al. 2018; Offerman et al. 2022; Lopez-Fernandez et al. 2022, moderate confidence).

hybrid.label: Defined hybrid (phase gates + iterations)
hybrid.rationale: Plan-driven governance with iterative delivery inside phases; suited to large or multi-team projects when coordination and planning between team and programme levels are designed in (Table 4.5; Findings 2.2, 3.3, 4.4), and acceptable under regulation with explicit assurance gates (Finding 2.3).

caveats.message: Team maturity is low: invest in training, coaching, management support and change management before and during adoption, whichever methodology is chosen (Dikert et al., 2016; McKenzie et al., 2021; Uludag et al., 2019; Table 4.5, high confidence).

Strict regulation: plan documentation, verification and certification evidence explicitly within the iterative process; adapted agile processes have met such demands (Ribeiro et al., 2025; Smith et al., 2019), but the evidence is limited (Table 4.5, low confidence).

Strict regulation: a plan-driven process is one acceptable option, but the limited evidence also supports adapted agile or hybrid processes with explicit assurance gates (Table 4.5, Finding 2.3, low confidence).

Large or multi-team project: design coordination across teams (roles, meetings, shared artefacts) and align planning between team and programme levels, whichever approach is used (Kula et al., 2022; Berntzen et al., 2023; Bick et al., 2018; Table 4.5, high confidence).
High requirement volatility: late changes are costly in a sequential process; add prototyping and iterative testing (Boehm, 2002; Table 4.5, F1.1).
Distributed team: invest in strong asynchronous communication and documentation to offset reduced face-to-face coordination (design assumption, change C1).
